lesson.title: Screens Are Tools: My Daily Tech Budget, With a Guide
lesson.topic: Set a daily cap on screen time for learning (about 1 to 1.5 hours), use screens as tools rather than entertainment, and have an adult guide check in.
lesson.steelman: Is more technology always better for learning?
lesson.steelman_for: A clear cap keeps screens as a tool for practice and research, leaving time for hands-on work, people and outdoors.
lesson.steelman_against: Some learners do great work on screens (coding, design), and a hard cap can feel arbitrary without a reason they agree with.
lesson.example: Imagine Priya, 10, who writes down every time she uses a tablet for a day. She sorts each use into 'tool' or 'fun', then agrees with her guide on 75 minutes of tool time and a timer she sets herself.
lesson.activity: For one day, keep a screen log (what, why, how long). Sort each item into Tool or Fun. With your guide, set tomorrow's tool-time budget and one rule for when the budget runs out.
check_questions: What is the difference between a screen used as a tool and as entertainment?
Why might an adult guide help with a screen budget?
What will you do when your budget runs out?

rationale: Acton Academy's 1-1.5 hour tech limit and Alpha School's guides-not-lecturers model (2026-10-25 scan); the learner helps set the cap, so it is self-management, not just a rule.
